items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: In the trumpet section, we had on first trumpet Gail Brockman.

ctx.x: on second tenor. On first tenor we had Lucky Thompson. On baritone, we had a young fellow who before had been playing alto saxophone, but he wanted to get in the band when the band was being organized, so Billy Eckstine asked him if he would play baritone saxophone, and he agreed to do it, and Billy bought him a baritone, and so he became the baritone saxophone player. [LEO PARKER] So those were the five saxophones.

In the trumpet section, we had on first trumpet Gail Brockman. On second trumpet, Buddy Anderson, a fine, fine trumpet player. Buddy Anderson was from Oklahoma City, but he had come from Jay McShann's band, as well as Charlie Parker. Buddy Anderson played second trumpet. Shorty McConnell, formerly with the Earl Hines band, played third trumpet. And fourth trumpet was Dizzy Gillespie.

And the trombone section... This is where my memory kind of goes blank. I can't remember, because that section changed around quite a bit. One of the main people in the trombone section that I remember was the arranger.... I don't know why I can't remember his name, because as well as I know it... Gerald Valentine! Jerry Valentine. Which is another guy that I learned a hell of a lot from about arranging. Jerry Valentine did most of the arrangements of the band. And I might add that he could write faster and come…
